ものだ.en: ものだ is used for general observations like 'that’s how it is' or 'naturally so'. It doesn't function as advice or a command. We are looking for a grammar point that is used to highlight a desire or a weak command.

はずだ.en: はずだ expresses certainty ('bound to be'), not give advice. We are looking for a grammar point that is used to highlight a desire or a weak command.

attributes.translation: Because there is an important game tomorrow, you should practice.
attributes.nuance_translation: A particle construction that is often used for presenting orders or expectations from an authority.

attributes.content: 先輩（せんぱい）、後輩（こうはい）はもっと大切（たいせつ）にする____。
attributes.translation: Senpai you should treat your kouhai with great care.

attributes.body_ja:
終助詞（しゅうじょし）の「こと」には主（おも）に二（ふた）つの使（つか）い方（かた）があります。

１．願望（がんぼう）や軽（かる）い命令（めいれい）を表（あらわ）す 。

２．感嘆（かんたん）や疑問（ぎもん）を表（あらわ）す。

ここでは、一（ひと）つ目（め）の使（つか）い方（かた）を学（まな）びましょう。二（ふた）つ目（め）の「こと」は、主（おも）に女性（じょせい）が使（つか）う表現（ひょうげん）で、現代（げんだい）ではあまり使（つか）われません。

「こと」は、「(A) するべきだ」や「(A) するべきじゃない」と注意（ちゅうい）やアドバイスをしたいときに使（つか）われます。動詞（どうし）の辞書形（じしょけい）（またはナイ形（けい））のあとに付（つ）けて、文（ぶん）の終（お）わりに使（つか）います。「こと」のあとには助動詞（じょどうし）の「だ」を付（つ）けることが多（おお）いですが、絶対（ぜったい）ではありません。

注意点（ちゅういてん）

この「こと」には軽（かる）い命令（めいれい）のニュアンスがあるので、ルールや注意書（ちゅういが）きなどでよく使（つか）われます（お店（みせ）や公園（こうえん）のポスターなど）。目上（めうえ）の人（ひと）にアドバイスをするときには使（つか）わない方（ほう）がいいでしょう。
attributes.body:
As a sentence ending particle, こと has two primary functions. These are as follows:

願望（がんぼう）や軽（かる）い命令（めいれい）を表（あらわ）す - Highlighting a desire or weak command.

感嘆（かんたん）や疑問（ぎもん）を表（あらわ）す - Highlighting astonishment or doubt.

We will focus on the first meaning in this grammar point, as the 'astonishment' nuance is not as commonly used in modern Japanese, and is primarily used only by women.

At the end of a sentence, こと will be paired with the dictionary (or ない) form of a verb, to highlight a particular action that either should, or should not occur. It is usually grouped with the auxiliary verb だ, although this is not always the case. This construction is most often translated as 'should/should not (A)', or 'ought to/not (A)'.

Caution

This use of こと implies a certain level of 'authority', and is therefore regularly used in relation to set rules and expectations (can very frequently be seen on signs in shops/parks, etc). Due to this, it should not be used when giving 'general' advice, especially to people of higher status.

attributes.description: Should: ほうがいい、べき、ことだ

attributes.body: The imperative or command form  (命令形) gives direct, blunt commands, e.g. 止まれ ('Stop!'). It can sound harsh unless softened with particles like よ, e.g. 頑張れよ ('Try harder, okay?'). In contrast, ことだ offers soft advice, e.g. 早起きすることだ ('You should wake up early.'), and is often used when giving recommendations or suggestions.

ことだ suggests what one should do as advice or a general guideline, e.g. 無理をしないことだ ('You should take it easy.') べきではない expresses the opposite, indicating what one should not do based on moral or social expectations, e.g. 人を見た目で判断すべきではない ('You shouldn't judge people by appearances.')

second_relatable.title: べきではない
second_relatable.meaning: Should not, Must not , Ought not to

attributes.body: ことはない downplays the need for action and is often used to reassure, e.g. 焦ることはない ('There's no need to rush.') ことだ gives firm advice and carries an authoritative tone, e.g. 焦らずに進めることだ ('You should proceed calmly.') ことはない can also mean that something never occurs, which is a usage unrelated to ことだ, e.g. 彼と会うことはない ('I never see him.')

first_relatable.title: ことはない
first_relatable.meaning: There is no need to, Never happens

attributes.body: Both can be used to give advice or suggestions, but the tone differs. ことだ sounds more formal or authoritative, as if stating a rule or guideline. In contrast, ばいい is more casual and conversational, often used among friends. Additionally, ばいい can be used in contrary-to-fact suggestions, such as 行けばいいのに ('You should go but you won't'). ことだ cannot be used this way.

second_relatable.title: ばいい
second_relatable.meaning: Can, Should, It'd be good if

attributes.body: Both express what should be done, but with different nuance. ことだ is used to give firm advice, e.g. 諦めずに続けることだ ('You should keep going without giving up.') ものだ expresses general expectations or norms, e.g. 仕事は地道に頑張り続けるものだ ('One is expected to keep working steadily.')

second_relatable.title: ものだ
second_relatable.meaning: Supposed to, Should, That's the way it is

attributes.body: Both express obligation, but differ in tone. ことだ is used to offer advice or general suggestions, e.g. 無理をしないことだ ('You should take it easy.') べき is stronger, implying moral or logical necessity, e.g. 約束は守るべきだ ('You should keep your promises.')

Both express reasoning in a broad sense, but are used differently. わけだ explains why something is the case, e.g. 暖房が壊れているのか。だから寒いわけだ ('So the heater's broken. That explains why it's cold.') ことだ gives strong advice or instruction, e.g. 寒いなら暖房をつけることだ ('If it's cold, you should turn on the heater.')

first_relatable.title: わけだ
first_relatable.meaning: For that reason, No wonder, As you'd expect, Naturally, Thus, This is why

attributes.body: Both carry an authoritative tone, as if stating a rule, but have opposite meanings. ことだ gives strong advice or recommendations, e.g. 約束は守ることだ ('You should keep your promises.') てはならない expresses strict prohibition, e.g. 約束を破ってはならない ('You must not break your promises.')

たほうがいい is a common expression used top give advice or make suggestions, often reflecting the speaker's personal opinion on what would be better. ことだ may appear similar but is more formal, carrying a stronger nuance of expectation, implying 'this is how things are (or should be,' rather than a personal suggestion.

first_relatable.title: たほうがいい
first_relatable.meaning: It'd be better to, Should do

attributes.body: ないほうがいい is used to suggest not doing something, similar to 'You shouldn't…' in English. It's a common expression that often reflects the speaker's personal or subjective opinion. In contrast, ことだ expresses the opposite idea, meaning 'should' or 'ought to,' and is more formal. It carries the nuance of stating a rule or general expectation rather than personal advice.

first_relatable.title: ないほうがいい
first_relatable.meaning: It'd be better not to, Shouldn't do

attributes.body: ことだ is used for light advice ('should' or 'ought to'), e.g. 毎日早起きすることだ ('You should get up early every day.'). なければならない expresses stronger obligation, like 'must' or 'have to', often implying consequences. ７時に起きなければならない ('You must get up at 7.').
